user.title: Set up Free Library Events
user.description: Create an age-based event selection from Free Library of Philadelphia feeds. Choose the person and branches here, then use Configure for matching, refresh timing, and calendar subscriptions. One integration entry is supported.

data_description.child_name: Use a name of up to 80 characters for the digest heading. It stays in Home Assistant unless you share the generated digest.
data_description.birth_date: Age is calculated separately for each event date. Home Assistant uses it to choose library age feeds and apply matching rules; requests contain age categories, not the birth date or name.
data_description.branches: Choose one or more of the four listed branches. The integration fetches events for these branches.

init.title: Configure Free Library Events
init.description:
Choose which settings to change. To change the person or selected branches, open Reconfigure on the integration entry.

Calendar subscription: {webcal_status}

behavior.title: Matching and timing
behavior.description: Set how broadly events match the person’s age, how calendar entries handle missing end times, and when Home Assistant fetches library feeds. Matching uses feed content and local rules; check event eligibility with the library.

data_description.filter_mode: Strict accepts the strongest matches from age ranges, library categories, or event wording. Recommended also accepts inclusive wording and possible matches. Broad additionally accepts general children’s or family wording. These rules help select events; they do not establish eligibility.
data_description.calendar_duration_minutes: When an event has no parsed end time, calendar entries and Google Calendar links use this duration. Default: 60 minutes. This supplies an end time for the calendar; it does not establish the event’s actual duration.
data_description.scan_interval_seconds: Home Assistant fetches feeds every 21600 seconds (6 hours) by default. Refresh events and the digest action can request a fetch sooner. Subscription requests use cached events, and the subscribing app decides when to check again.

webcal.title: Calendar subscription
webcal.description:
Share the filtered event cache as a read-only calendar feed. Anyone who has its URL can read it without a Home Assistant login. The feed includes event details and the calendar name below. It does not include the person’s display name or birth date. Calendar apps choose their own refresh schedule.

Current subscription: {webcal_status}

data_description.publish_webcal: Disabled initially. Enabling shows the URL for review before the final save. Saving with this switched off removes the access token and disables the URL; copies already held by calendar apps can remain.
data_description.webcal_name: Use 1–80 characters for the name supplied in the feed. A calendar app may display a subscriber’s own name instead.

regenerate_webcal.title: Regenerate calendar subscription URL
regenerate_webcal.description: Continue to create a replacement subscription URL. The existing URL remains active until you save on the next screen. After saving, update each calendar subscription to use the new URL. Events already copied into a calendar app can remain.

render_digest.name: Render weekly digest
render_digest.description: Builds subject, message, html, and metadata for a Monday–Sunday event digest. On Mondays it uses the week starting that day; otherwise it uses the coming week. Pass the response to a notification action to send it.

force_refresh.name: Refresh first
force_refresh.description: Request a feed refresh before rendering (default: on). If that refresh fails, the action returns an error. Turn this off to use the existing cache, which may be older; rendering still requires fetched data.

embed_images.name: Embed event images
embed_images.description: Download event images for inline email use and add images and attachments to the response (default: off). Modern SMTP attachments require Local Media; without it, the attachments list is empty. Pass the matching response fields to your notification action. Cleanup is scheduled after one hour, so send promptly. Some images may remain remote or be omitted; display depends on the email client.

library_data_unavailable.message: No fetched event data is available to render. Use Refresh events and inspect the Status sensor, then retry after a successful fetch.

library_refresh_failed.message: The requested refresh failed and the digest was not rendered. Inspect the Status sensor for the latest attempt and retry after the feed issue is resolved.

settings_changed_during_render.message: The settings or loaded integration changed while the action was waiting for a refresh. Run the digest action again to use the current configuration.

manual_refresh_failed.message: Refresh events could not complete successfully. Inspect the Status sensor’s latest attempt and last successful fetch before trying again.

library_source_update_failed.message: Every source request failed in this attempt. Automatic refreshes can retry; any event cache from an earlier fetch has not been updated.

single_loaded_entry_required.message: The digest action needs exactly one loaded Free Library Events entry. Check the integration’s setup status before running it again.
